newsitem.title: USA: Kevorkian attends Tennessee man's suicide.
newsitem.headline: Kevorkian attends Tennessee man's suicide.

text.p: Dr. Jack Kevorkian attended his 39th suicide Monday night, the death of a 73-year-old Tennessee man suffering from pancreatic cancer.
Attorney Geoffrey Fieger said Kevorkian brought the body of Jack Leatherman of Knoxville, Tennessee, to William Beaumont Hospital in Royal Oak, Michigan.
Fieger declined to provide details about the location and cause of Leatherman's death.
The suicide was the sixth that Kevorkian has attended within the past month and the 39th he has acknowledged since starting his crusade for doctor-assisted suicide in 1990.
The month of August, with five suicides, was his biggest since February 1993, just before a now-expired law against assisted suicide went into effect.

Nearly all of Kevorkian's recent patients have travelled to Michigan from other states to end their lives. The 68-year-old retired pathologist is still battling criticism in the August 15 death of Judith Curren, of Pembroke, Massachusetts, who suffered from chronic fatigue syndrome and had lodged abuse charges against her husband.
At about 8 p.m. EDT Monday night, Kevorkian drove up to Beaumont Hospital's emergency room entrance with Leatherman's body in the back seat of his car, said hospital spokeswoman Colette Stimmell.

"The body was removed from the car and brought into the emergency room," Stimmell said. Kevorkian then "handed the physician a three-by-five card with the person's name, age, diagnosis and insurance information on it. Shortly after that, he left," she said.
No attempt was made to revive the body, she said, adding it had been transferred to the Oakland County Medical Examiner for an autopsy.

Fieger told the Oakland Press in Tuesday's edition that Leatherman had been a patient of Kevorkian's since he was first diagnosed with cancer in May. Leatherman had asked his personal physician to help him die but the physician refused, Fieger told the Pontiac, Mich., newspaper.
